- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or neutral (0.00), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for downward momentum.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 5–10% in the following 2–3 periods.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline after peak), model often fails to adjust; apply a “reversion buffer” — cap forecast at 10–15% below recent peak.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to short-term sentiment shifts; use a “sentiment smoothing” rule — average sentiment over 3–5 days before adjusting forecast.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with trend; prioritize trend-following only if sentiment is consistent for 3+ days.
